main:
Capabilities
/
Prototype machining
Machined prototypes for your next revision

Machined prototypes for design development. Browse examples and discuss the next revision of your part.

Prepare RFQ email
Ring housings & angled components
What should your prototype verify?

Prototype examples focus on automotive housings and intake or cooling components. State the goal: packaging, assembly, appearance or a specific functional test. A prototype does not automatically validate a production design.

Geometry & process
For checking fit, assembly and design details before repeat production. STEP or IGES review helps identify tool access, fitment and manufacturability issues before machining. Automotive development examples include intercoolers, billet engine covers, intake manifolds, plenums and electronic throttle bodies.
Size & workholding
Send the current model revision, overall dimensions and stock size. Separate fixed interfaces from geometry still open to change so tool access and clamping space can be reviewed for the prototype.
Material & finish
Specify the material grade, condition and required finish. State whether production material and finish are essential to the evaluation, or whether alternatives may be proposed for your approval. Separate fit-check dimensions from appearance finishes.
Make the sample answer a design question
More part examples
Browse all parts
Aluminum intercooler prototypes
Billet aluminum engine covers
Drawing & acceptance
Drawing requirements

Identify the current revision and dimensions needed for the prototype evaluation. Separate fixed interfaces from geometry still open to change.

State whether production material and finish are essential to the evaluation, or whether alternatives may be proposed for your approval.

Inspection and acceptance

Agree the measurements and evidence needed to judge the prototype against its objective. Document the acceptance criteria for each critical interface.

If testing is required, identify who supplies the fixture and test procedure and who evaluates the result. No test completion is implied by the example.

Agree the measurement method and required records before production.

7–14 business days — Production, from 1 piece. Production starts after drawing and order confirmation. The period includes surface finishing; shipping time is additional.

Quality & inspection
Equipment and order records
Prepare your prototype machining enquiry

Provide the model, key drawing dimensions, prototype quantity, revision status and intended evaluation.

Explain any planned next revision or later batch. Give your requested date so it can be assessed; delivery still needs confirmation.

Prepare RFQ email

Add your requirements to the email draft, then attach drawings in your email app before sending.
